posts.title: Quick thinking store employee helps prevent impaired driving incident
posts.description: (ESPANOLA, ON)- Manitoulin OPP lays multiple charges following impaired driving investigation. On Saturday, November 21, 2026, at approximately 3:30 a.m., members of the Manitoulin Detachment of the Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) responded to a report of two individuals who appeared to be impaired at a gas station on Highway 17 in Baldwin Township. Officers arrived and located the vehicle still parked at the gas station. During the investigation, police observed signs of drug impairment displayed by the driver and located a small quantity of suspected cocaine. As a result, Hunter SERVICE, 26 years old, of Sudbury, was charged with: Operation while impaired - drugs Possession of a Schedule I substance - cocaine Drive vehicle or boat with cannabis readily available Driver fail to surrender licence Fail to surrender insurance card Drive motor vehicle in contravention of conditions In addition to the charges, the accused received a 90-day Administrative Driver's Licence Suspension (ADLS),

posts.title: Kaboni Day School students come together for impromptu reunion
posts.description: Click here to have Manitoulin news direct to your email. KABONI—Every parent wants their child to feel good about going to school, but sometimes we do not know how to process what is happening to our children. Neither do they. Imagine for the children and parents, back in 1947, when the Kaboni school was built, a time when the parents and children did not speak a word of English. This was the dilemma for many—to send or not send their child to a strange house of education, the Kaboni Day School. Former student Margaret Jackson of the little Kaboni Day School decided to make a random roll call and see who would answer. Well, to the delight of all, seven former students returned. I was invited to take pictures for posterity and gather some of their stories. First and foremost, I wish to share the translation of Kaboni as taught to me by my Nokomis, Jane Zack (nee Manitowabi). posts.title: Two Manitoulin First Nations reimagine education through culture, belonging and self-determination
posts.description: Click here to have Manitoulin news direct to your email. THUNDER BAY—“Every child has a gift. It’s our job to find [that] gift. And the only way to do that is to get to know our children.” There is something quietly revolutionary about those words, particularly when spoken by First Nations educators preparing to open the doors of a new school. For generations, Indigenous children were expected to bend themselves to the demands of educational institutions that too often failed to recognize their languages, cultures, ways of knowing and individual needs. For children who learned differently, those expectations could create yet another barrier to belonging. Now, two small First Nations on Manitoulin Island are working together to turn that history on its head.
